_comment: Source datasets researched for world dish roles and eating habits.
NOT yet wired into the app. Recorded here so the provenance of any future import is
traceable, and so the classification rules in scripts/classify-recipe-roles.mjs can be
checked against real-world data rather than guessed.
SOURCES
1. oxai/world-wide-dishes (GitHub, not Kaggle)
https://github.com/oxai/world-wide-dishes
The closest match to what we need. Columns include:
type_of_dish        e.g. "Main dish - eaten with sides"
type_of_dish_more   free-text detail
time_of_day          e.g. ["lunch", "dinner"]
time_of_day_more
countries, continent, regions, cultures, occasions, utensils, ingredients
Directly answers 'which are main courses and which are side dishes' and
'when is this eaten'. Licence must be confirmed before importing.
2. worldcuisines/food-kb (HuggingFace, mirrors the Kaggle world-cuisines work)
https://huggingface.co/datasets/worldcuisines/food-kb
~2.4k dishes with coarse_categories (stew, soup, rice, dessert), fine_categories
(curry, fried rice, rice cake), cuisines, countries, region1/region2 (UN M49 regions).
Good for seeding a new region pack's dish list and cuisine tagging.
3. Kaggle - Food Lovers: Global Cuisine Preferences Survey
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/themadprogramer/food-lovers-global-cuisine-preferences-survey
CC0 public domain. Geolocated responses on cuisine preference and availability.
Useful for 'what does a household here actually eat', not for dish roles.
4. Kaggle - Collection of Recipes around the world
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/prajwaldongre/collection-of-recipes-around-the-world
recipe_name, cuisine, ingredients, prep/cook minutes, servings, calories,
dietary_restrictions. Shape matches RegionRecipe closely, but has no dish role,
so it would need the same classification applied.
5. Kaggle - Open Food Facts / World Food Facts
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/openfoodfacts/world-food-facts
ODL. Packaged-product nutrition, 356k rows. Already conceptually covered by the OCR
label parser, so lower priority.
6. Kaggle competitions - What's Cooking? / Cuisine Classification Challenge
https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/whats-cooking/data
Recipe id + cuisine + ingredient list. Useful for cuisine inference on a recipe
with no cuisine tag. Competition rules apply to redistribution.
GAP IN THESE SOURCES
None of them provide a per-dish 'side dish' flag for Nepali food specifically, and
none pair a dish with a meal time the way we model it. The Nepal Bagmati roles are
therefore classified from its own category taxonomy, which is more reliable for the
launch region than a general-world guess. Any import should be treated as a seed for
future region packs, reviewed rather than trusted outright.

_roleVocabulary.mainCourse: A complete meal on its own. The only role eligible for a meal recommendation.
_roleVocabulary.sideDish: Served alongside a main course. Never recommended on its own.
_roleVocabulary.both: E.g. a rice dish that works as the meal and as an accompaniment.

_observedTypeOfDishValues.note: Verbatim examples of type_of_dish seen in source 1, useful as an import mapping.
